This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Vijaykumar A.Patil, J., Made The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimants/appellants seeking enhancement of the compensation against the Judgment and award dated 12.10.2018 passed in MVC No.47/2016 by the MACT No.XII, Ballari (for short hereinafter referred to as 'the tribunal').

2. Brief facts giving rise for filing of this appeal are that, on 09.07.2014 at about 7.30 p.m., the deceased B.Srinivasulu after completion of his work was returning from Guntakal on his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-03/BN-9140 by following the traffic rules on proper side of the road and when he reached near Beldona village NC: 2023:KHC-D:13211-DB of Chippagiri Mandalam, at that time, the driver of Auto bearing registration No.AP.02/TB.6715 i.e. respondent No.1 driving the B.Rojamam W/O.

Late B.Srinivasulu vs Gandodi Ramesh Babu S/O G Balappa on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14023600/
2 same in rash and negligent manner and dashed the motorcycle, resultantly the deceased B.
Srinivasulu sustained grievous injuries and later succumbed to the injuries.

entities.text: Late B.Srinivasulu vs Gandodi Ramesh Babu
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is averred that, prior to the accident the deceased B.Srinivasulu was hale and healthy and the Claimant No.1 is the wife,
claimant Nos.2 and 3 are the minor daughters and claimant No.4 is the mother of the deceased and were entirely dependent on his income.
It is also averred that, the deceased B.Srinivasulu was earning Rs.1,50,000/- per annum from agricultural work.
Hence, the claimants have filed the claim petition before the tribunal seeking compensation.
3. The respondent No.1 i.e. driver cum owner of the offending vehicle i.e. Auto bearing registration No.AP- 02/TB-6715 has not appeared before the tribunal and has been placed ex-parte.

The respondent No.2-Insurance company has filed written statement contending that, the NC:
2023:KHC-D:13211-DB accident was caused due to the negligent act of the deceased himself, but not due to the negligent act of the respondent No.1.

It was averred that, the respondent No.1 was not having driving licence to drive the said Auto as on the date of the accident and has not produced the driving licence, has violated the conditions of the motor vehicles Act, 1988 and sought to dismiss the claim petition.
4. The tribunal has framed the issues and recorded the evidence of the parties.
The appellant No.1 has examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.
The Manager Legal, of the Insurance company has examined himself as R.W.1 and got marked Ex.R.1.

The tribunal on considering the evidence available on record has awarded total compensation of Rs.15,69,400/-
with interest at the rate of 7% per annum.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, the claimants are in appeal.

5. Sri. Y. Lakshmikant Reddy, learned counsel appearing for the appellants submits that, the deceased NC: 2023:KHC-D:13211-DB was aged about 30 years, was an agriculturist and was earning Rs.1,50,000/- per annum, however the tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/-.
It is submitted that, the tribunal has also committed an error in not awarding consortium to the other appellants.
It is submitted that, the tribunal has awarded lower compensation on other heads and he seeks to enhance the same.

6. Per contra, Sri. S.K.Kayakmath, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance company supports the impugned Judgment and award and submits that, the appellants have failed to produce any evidence to substantiate the income of the deceased.

It is submitted that, the award of compensation by the tribunal on other heads are just and proper and does not call for any enhancement and accordingly, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.
7.

Having heard the learned counsels for the parties, perused the memorandum of appeal and the NC: 2023:KHC-D:13211-DB tribunal records, the point that arises for our consideration in these appeals are;
Whether the appellants-claimants are entitled for higher compensation?

8. The answer to the above point is in the affirmative for the following reason:
B.Rojamam W/O. Late B.Srinivasulu vs Gandodi Ramesh Babu S/O G Balappa on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14023600/
3 (a) The parties to the proceeding do not dispute that, one Sri. B. Srinivasulu died in the road accident dated 09.07.2014 and he was an agriculturist, was aged about 30 years at the time of accident.
The tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/-, as the appellant/claimants have not produced any evidence to substantiate the claim for income of Rs.1,50,000/- per annum.

In the absence of any evidence on record, this Court and Lok Adalaths normally rely on the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority to assess the notional income of the deceased in the road accident cases.

The accident is of the year 2014 a n d a s p e r t h e c h a r t r e f e r r e d s u p r a , t h e n o t i o n a l i n c o m e o f N C :
2023:KHC-D:13211-DB the deceased is required to be assessed at Rs.7,500/- as against Rs.7,000/-.
(b) The appellants are entitled for addition of 40% to the assessed income of the deceased under the head of loss of future prospects of the deceased.
The tribunal has rightly deducted 1/4th towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased and applied '17' multiplier.
(c) Each of the appellants i.e. wife, two daughters and mother are entitle for compensation under the head of loss of consortium.

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram, reported in (2018) SCC 130, each of the appellants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- under the head of loss of consortium.

sentences.text: The tribunal has rightly awarded compensation for loss of estate and transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
The same is unaltered.

The appellants are entitled for the following compensation at the rate of 6%:
Loss of dependency : Rs.7,500/- + 40% (Rs.3,000/-) = Rs.10,500/- minus 1/4th (Rs.2,625/-) = Rs.7,875/-
Rs.7,875/- X 12 X 17 = Rs.16,06,500/-

Loss of dependency Rs.16,06,500/-
2 Towards transportation of dead body Rs.30,000/-
and funeral expenses 3 Loss of consortium (4 X Rs.40,000/-) Rs.1,60,000/-

Total Rs.17,96,500/-

4 9.
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.17,96,500/- as against Rs.15,69,400/- awarded by the Tribunal.
10. Hence, we pass the following order.
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The judgment and award dated 12.10.2018 passed in MVC No.47/2016 by the MACT- XII, Ballari,
is modified to the extent that the claimants would be entitled to total NC: 2023:KHC-D:13211-DB compensation of Rs.17,96,500/- as against Rs.15,69,400/- awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till date of payment.
iv. Respondent/Insurance Company shall
deposit the enhanced compensation amount along with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
v. Registry to transmit the records to the Tribunal forthwith.

vi. Draw modified award accordingly.
